claim: Myocardial infarction (MI) is accompanied by severe energy deprivation and extensive epigenetic changes.
source: Myocardial infarction (MI) is accompanied by severe energy deprivation and extensive epigenetic changes.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a known characteristic of MI, supported by the broader scientific literature on MI pathophysiology.

claim: Elevation of acetyl-CoA by sodium octanoate (8C) significantly improved heart function in ischemia reperfusion (I/R) rats.
source: we examined the effect of different carbon sources that are involved in the major metabolic pathways of acetyl-CoA synthesis on myocardial infarction and found that elevation of acetyl-CoA by sodium octanoate (8C) significantly improved heart function in ischemia reperfusion (I/R) rats.
evidence: The abstract states this finding directly, which is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript including infarct size measurements and echocardiography results.

claim: 8C reduced I/R injury by promoting histone acetylation which in turn activated the expression of antioxidant genes and inhibited cardiomyocyte (CM) apoptosis.
source: Mechanistically, 8C reduced I/R injury by promoting histone acetylation which in turn activated the expression of antioxidant genes and inhibited cardiomyocyte (CM) apoptosis.
evidence: This mechanistic claim is supported by multiple experimental results including histone acetylation measurements, gene expression analysis, and apoptosis assays presented in the manuscript.

claim: 8C-promoted histone acetylation and heart repair were carried out by metabolic enzyme medium-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase (MCAD) and histone acetyltransferase Kat2a.
source: Furthermore, we elucidated that 8C-promoted histone acetylation and heart repair were carried out by metabolic enzyme medium-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase (MCAD) and histone acetyltransferase Kat2a
evidence: This is supported by knockdown experiments showing that depletion of either MCAD or Kat2a abolished the protective effects of 8C.

claim: Myocardial infarction (MI) is one of the leading causes of death in the world.
source: Myocardial infarction (MI), which blocks the supply of energy to infarcted area, is one of the leading causes of death in the world Pagidipati and Gaziano, 2013.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Pagidipati and Gaziano, 2013.

claim: A bi-directional interplay between metabolism and epigenetic control has been proposed: metabolism directly regulates chromatin epigenetic state, whereas chromatin state defines gene control in response to metabolic status.
source: Notably, a bi-directional interplay between metabolism and epigenetic control has been proposed recently: metabolism directly regulates chromatin epigenetic state, whereas chromatin state defines gene control in response to metabolic status Pietrocola et al., 2015; Shi and Tu, 2015.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Pietrocola et al., 2015 and Shi and Tu, 2015.

claim: Acetyl-CoA is an intermediary metabolite that serves as an energy-providing substrate and is also used by histone acetyltransferases (HATs) to transfer the acetyl-group to histone residues for histone acetylation.
source: Acetyl-CoA, an intermediary metabolite that serves as an energy-providing substrate, is also used by histone acetyltransferases (HATs) to transfer the acetyl-group to histone residues for histone acetylation Cai et al., 2011; Wellen et al., 2009.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Cai et al., 2011 and Wellen et al., 2009.

claim: Manipulation of acetyl-CoA, either by intervention of synthetic enzymes, or nutrient source could alter histone acetylation in various cell types.
source: Manipulation of acetyl-CoA, either by intervention of synthetic enzymes, or nutrient source could alter histone acetylation in various cell types Wellen et al., 2009; Sutendra et al., 2014; Zhao et al., 2016; McDonnell et al., 2016.
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations: Wellen et al., 2009; Sutendra et al., 2014; Zhao et al., 2016; McDonnell et al., 2016.

claim: Myocardial ischemia reperfusion (I/R) injury causes dramatic metabolism changes and subsequent histone deacetylation.
source: Moreover, myocardial ischemia reperfusion (I/R) injury causes dramatic metabolism changes and subsequent histone deacetylation.
evidence: This is stated as a known phenomenon in the introduction, drawing on established knowledge in the field.

claim: Inhibition of histone deacetylation activity protects heart function after I/R injury.
source: Inhibition of histone deacetylation activity protects heart function after I/R injury Tian et al., 2019; Xie et al., 2014
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Tian et al., 2019 and Xie et al., 2014.

claim: Inhibition of histone deacetylation inhibits cardiac remodeling and heart failure.
source: inhibits cardiac remodeling and heart failure Jeong et al., 2018.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Jeong et al., 2018.

claim: Among the five metabolites examined (2C, 3C, 6C, 8C, 9C), 2C, 3C, and 8C significantly reduced the IS/AAR ratio, whereas 6C and 9C treatment did not reduce IS/AAR ratio compared to saline-treated groups.
source: Among the five metabolites examined, 2C, 3C, and 8C significantly reduced the IS/AAR ratio, whereas 6C and 9C treatment did not reduce IS/AAR ratio compared to saline-treated groups (Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A-B).
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A-B.

claim: 8C administration at the time of reperfusion reduced the IS/AAR ratio from 72% to 52% compared to saline control after I/R at 24 hr after reperfusion.
source: Evans blue/TTC staining showed that 24 hr after reperfusion, 8C administration reduced the IS/AAR ratio from 72% to 52% compared to saline control after I/R (Figure 1E–F and Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This specific quantitative finding is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 1E-F and Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: 8C administration led to increase of EF and FS from 47% to 58% and 24% to 31%, respectively, compared to saline treated I/R rats at 24 hr after I/R.
source: Compared to saline treated I/R rats, 8C administration led to increase of EF and FS from 47% to 58% and 24% to 31%, respectively (Figure 1G–H and Figure 1—figure supplement 1D)
evidence: This specific quantitative finding is stated in the text and supported by echocardiography data in Figure 1G-H and Figure 1—figure supplement 1D.

claim: There was a significant reduction of acetyl-CoA concentration in hearts after I/R.
source: Importantly, we found that there was a significant reduction of acetyl-CoA concentration in hearts after I/R, while 8C administration increased acetyl-CoA level in hearts after I/R (Figure 1I).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by acetyl-CoA measurements shown in Figure 1I.

claim: 8C administration increased acetyl-CoA level in hearts after I/R.
source: Importantly, we found that there was a significant reduction of acetyl-CoA concentration in hearts after I/R, while 8C administration increased acetyl-CoA level in hearts after I/R (Figure 1I).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by acetyl-CoA measurements shown in Figure 1I.

claim: 8C administration elevated H3K9ac level in hearts after I/R.
source: Moreover, 8C administration elevated H3K9ac level in hearts after I/R (Figure 1J–K).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 1J-K.

claim: A single dose of 8C administration at the time of reperfusion is beneficial for long-term cardiac function after I/R at 4 weeks.
source: Furthermore, to investigate whether a single dose of 8C administration is beneficial for long-term cardiac function after I/R, we examined the infarct size and heart function at 4 weeks after I/R.
evidence: This is supported by data showing reduced infarct size and improved heart function at 4 weeks after I/R with 8C treatment (Figure 1L-O).

claim: 8C can quickly enter into cells and contribute to around 50% of acetyl-CoA in heart at one hour after administration.
source: Together with the fact that 8C can quickly enter into cells and contribute to around 50% of acetyl-CoA in heart at one hour after administration Walton et al., 2003
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Walton et al., 2003.

claim: 8C administration at the time of reperfusion elevated acetyl-CoA production and histone acetylation level and significantly improved both short-term and long-term cardiac function after I/R.
source: our results indicated that 8C administration at the time of reperfusion elevated acetyl-CoA production and histone acetylation level and significantly improved both short-term and long-term cardiac function after I/R.
evidence: This summary claim is supported by multiple experimental results presented in Figure 1, including acetyl-CoA measurements, histone acetylation levels, and cardiac function assessments at both 24 hr and 4 weeks.

claim: Apoptosis is one of the major reasons for cardiac damage after I/R injury.
source: Apoptosis is one of the major reasons for cardiac damage after I/R injury MacLellan and Schneider, 1997.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to MacLellan and Schneider, 1997.

claim: 8C treatment dramatically reduced TUNEL-positive cardiomyocytes in border zone after I/R.
source: 8C treatment dramatically reduced TUNEL-positive cardiomyocytes in border zone (Figure 2A, B).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by TUNEL staining data shown in Figure 2A-B.

claim: The levels of myocardial death marker cTnI, serum CK-MB as well as total CK and LDH were reduced in I/R rats after 8C administration.
source: Consistent with the TUNEL assay, the levels of myocardial death marker cTnI, serum CK-MB as well as total CK and LDH were also reduced in I/R rats after 8C administration (Figure 2C, D and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A-B).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by biochemical assay data shown in Figure 2C-D and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A-B.

claim: 8C led to reduction in pro-apoptotic regulator Bax and upregulation of anti-apoptotic gene Bcl2 at 24 hr after I/R injury.
source: Moreover, 8C led to reduction in pro-apoptotic regulator Bax and upregulation of anti-apoptotic gene Bcl2 at 24 hr after I/R injury (Figure 2E, F).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 2E-F.

claim: Genes involved in apoptotic signaling pathways were enriched in saline-treated compared to 8C-treated rats after I/R.
source: Gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) Subramanian et al., 2005 showed that genes involved in apoptotic signaling pathways were enriched in saline-treated compared to 8C-treated rats after I/R (Figure 2G).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by GSEA analysis shown in Figure 2G.

claim: I/R reduced the expression of anti-oxidative stress enzymes such as SOD1, SOD2, SOD3, CAT, Txnrd2, and Txnrd3, while 8C treatment upregulated the expression of these genes.
source: Specifically, I/R reduced the expression of anti-oxidative stress enzymes such as SOD1, SOD2, SOD3, CAT, Txnrd2, and Txnrd3, while 8C treatment upregulated the expression of these genes (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1E.

claim: I/R-induced oxidative stress triggers CM apoptosis after reperfusion.
source: Since I/R-induced oxidative stress triggers CM apoptosis after reperfusion Hausenloy and Yellon, 2013
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Hausenloy and Yellon, 2013.

claim: The intensity of DHE signal was significantly lower in the presence of 8C after I/R, indicating that 8C reduced oxidative stress after I/R.
source: The intensity of DHE signal was significantly lower in the presence of 8C after I/R (Figure 2H, I), indicating that 8C reduced oxidative stress after I/R.
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by DHE staining data shown in Figure 2H-I.

claim: 8C rescued the myocardial SOD activity after I/R.
source: Moreover, 8C rescued the myocardial SOD activity after I/R (Figure 2—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by SOD activity assay data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1F.

claim: One major mechanism through which 8C improved cardiac function after I/R was reduction of the oxidative stress and subsequent cell apoptosis.
source: Altogether, these results showed that one major mechanism through which 8C improved cardiac function after I/R was reduction of the oxidative stress and subsequent cell apoptosis.
evidence: This is a summary claim based on multiple experimental results showing reduced ROS, increased antioxidant gene expression, and decreased apoptosis with 8C treatment.

claim: 8C significantly reduced the percentage of apoptotic cells after sI/R in NRVMs, as evidenced by the lower percentage of Annexin V and PI double positive cells.
source: 8C significantly reduced the percentage of apoptotic cells, as evidenced by the lower percentage of Annexin V and PI double positive cells (Figure 3A, B).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by FACS analysis data shown in Figure 3A-B.

claim: 8C administration reduced cell death after sI/R as showed by increased cell viability and decreased LDH release into culture medium.
source: 8C administration reduced cell death after sI/R as showed by increased cell viability and decreased LDH release into to culture medium (Figure 3C, D).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by CCK8 and LDH assay data shown in Figure 3C-D.

claim: The expression of cleaved PARP was reduced with 8C administration after sI/R.
source: Moreover, the expression of cleaved PARP, which is a hallmark of apoptosis, was reduced with 8C administration (Figure 3E).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: The ROS level was significantly decreased in NRVMs with 8C treatment after sI/R.
source: The ROS level was significantly decreased in NRVMs with 8C treatment after sI/R (Figure 3F-H), indicating a direct effect of 8C in alleviating oxidative stress after sI/R.
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by DHE staining and FACS analysis data shown in Figure 3F-H.

claim: 8C reduced cardiomyocyte apoptosis through alleviating oxidative stress after sI/R.
source: Thus, our collective in vivo and in vitro results revealed that 8C reduced cardiomyocyte apoptosis through alleviating oxidative stress after sI/R.
evidence: This is a summary claim based on multiple in vivo and in vitro experimental results showing reduced apoptosis and oxidative stress with 8C treatment.

claim: 8C-generated acetyl-CoA contributes to histone acetylation in several cell types.
source: 8C-generated acetyl-CoA contributes to histone acetylation in several cell types McDonnell et al., 2016
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to McDonnell et al., 2016.

claim: Histone acetylation plays an important role in regulating cellular response to oxidative stress.
source: histone acetylation plays an important role in regulating cellular response to oxidative stress Shimazu et al., 2013.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Shimazu et al., 2013.

claim: sI/R reduced acetyl-CoA level in NRVMs and 8C significantly increased the production of acetyl-CoA in NRVMs.
source: Similar to in vivo I/R injury, sI/R reduced acetyl-CoA level in NRVMs and 8C significantly increased the production of acetyl-CoA in NRVMs (Figure 4A).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by acetyl-CoA measurements shown in Figure 4A.

claim: sI/R led to a remarkable decrease of H3K9ac, H3K14ac, H3K27ac, and acH3, and 8C increased histone acetylation in normal NRVMs and NRVMs under sI/R.
source: We found that sI/R led to a remarkable decrease of H3K9ac, H3K14ac, H3K27ac, and acH3, and that 8C increased histone acetylation in normal NRVMs and NRVMs under sI/R (Figure 4B–E).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 4B-E.

claim: 2C, 3C, and 8C could lead to upregulation of acH3 and H3K9ac level which was consistent with in vivo data that 2C, 3C and 8C but not 6C and 9C protected heart after I/R.
source: We found that 2C, 3C, and 8C could lead to upregulation of acH3 and H3K9ac level which was consistent with our in vivo data that 2C, 3C and 8C but not 6C and 9C protected heart after I/R (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: 8C, as well as 2C and 3C, likely reduced I/R injury through stimulating histone acetylation by acetyl-CoA production.
source: These results suggest that 8C, as well as 2C and 3C, likely reduced I/R injury through stimulating histone acetylation by acetyl-CoA production.
evidence: This is an inference based on the correlation between metabolites that increase histone acetylation and those that protect against I/R injury.

claim: C13 labeled acetyl-histones were detected in in vivo heart after MI.
source: Indeed, C13 labeled acetyl-histones were detected in in vivo heart after MI (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1D.

claim: 8C-produced acetyl-CoA contributed to epigenetic regulation of antioxidant genes in response to I/R injury.
source: Collectively, our results suggested that 8C-produced acetyl-CoA contributed to epigenetic regulation of antioxidant genes in response to I/R injury.
evidence: This is a summary claim based on multiple experimental results showing that 8C increases acetyl-CoA, histone acetylation at antioxidant gene promoters, and expression of these genes.

claim: MCAD is a key enzyme in the generation of acetyl-CoA from 8C.
source: we knocked down MCAD (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A), a key enzyme in the generation of acetyl-CoA from 8C Matsubara et al., 1986.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Matsubara et al., 1986.

claim: MCAD knockdown blocked the 8C-reduced cellular ROS level after sI/R.
source: Importantly, MCAD knockdown blocked the 8C-reduced cellular ROS level after sI/R (Figure 5C–D and Figure 5—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by DHE staining and FACS analysis data shown in Figure 5C-D and Figure 5—figure supplement 1C.

claim: MCAD knockdown reduced 8C-elevated expression of HO1 and NQO1 after sI/R.
source: Subsequently, MCAD knockdown reduced 8C-elevated expression of HO1 and NQO1 after sI/R (Figure 5F and Figure 5—figure supplement 1D-F).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by qPCR and Western blot data shown in Figure 5F and Figure 5—figure supplement 1D-F.

claim: Kat2a and Kat2b are the major HATs that modulate H3K9ac.
source: Kat2a and Kat2b are the major HATs that modulate H3K9ac Jin et al., 2011.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Jin et al., 2011.

claim: Kat2a is mostly responsive to acetyl-CoA concentrations at 0–10 µM.
source: Kat2a is mostly responsive to acetyl-CoA concentrations at 0–10 µM Wang et al., 2017
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Wang et al., 2017.

claim: Kat2b is response to acetyl-CoA in the 0–300 µM range.
source: while Kat2b is response to acetyl-CoA in the 0–300 µM range Shi et al., 2016.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Shi et al., 2016.

claim: Kat2a expression was upregulated in rat heart after I/R injury, whereas 8C treatment diminished Kat2a upregulation.
source: Kat2a expression was upregulated in rat heart after I/R injury, whereas 8C treatment diminished Kat2a upregulation (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Acetyl-CoA levels in NRVMs ranged from 1 to 7 µM under sI/R.
source: Together with the fact that acetyl-CoA levels in NRVMs ranged from 1 to 7 µM under sI/R (Figure 4A)
evidence: This is stated in the text and refers to data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Kat2a knockdown abolished 8C-stimulated H3K9ac increase at the promoters of HO1 and NQO1 after sI/R.
source: Specifically, Kat2a knockdown abolished 8C-stimulated H3K9ac increase at the promoters of HO1 and NQO1 after sI/R (Figure 6E).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 6E.

claim: Kat2a knockdown reduced 8C-elevated expression of HO1 and NQO1 after sI/R.
source: Subsequently, Kat2a knockdown reduced 8C-elevated expression of HO1 and NQO1 after sI/R (Figure 6F and Figure 6—figure supplement 1E-G).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by qPCR and Western blot data shown in Figure 6F and Figure 6—figure supplement 1E-G.

claim: 8C-stimulated histone acetylation leads to increase of antioxidant gene expression for heart repair.
source: Our study further reveals that 8C-stimulated histone acetylation leads to increase of antioxidant gene expression for heart repair.
evidence: This is a summary claim based on experimental results showing that 8C increases histone acetylation at antioxidant gene promoters and their expression.

claim: The study demonstrates systematically for the first time that modulating acetyl-CoA abundance can determine cardiomyocyte response to I/R injury via common metabolic and epigenetic mechanisms.
source: Our study demonstrates systematically for the first time that modulating acetyl-CoA abundance can determine cardiomyocyte response to I/R injury via common metabolic and epigenetic mechanisms.
evidence: This is a summary claim emphasizing the novelty of the study's findings.

claim: The study reveals a novel mechanism centered on acetyl-CoA that connects metabolic dynamics and epigenetic regulation in cardiac repair after I/R injury.
source: Our study reveals a novel mechanism centered on acetyl-CoA that connects metabolic dynamics and epigenetic regulation in cardiac repair after I/R injury and suggests that acetyl-CoA could be a survival signal for cardiomyocyte after I/R injury.
evidence: This is a summary claim emphasizing the novelty and significance of the study's findings.

claim: Acetyl-CoA could be a survival signal for cardiomyocyte after I/R injury.
source: Our study reveals a novel mechanism centered on acetyl-CoA that connects metabolic dynamics and epigenetic regulation in cardiac repair after I/R injury and suggests that acetyl-CoA could be a survival signal for cardiomyocyte after I/R injury.
evidence: This is a speculative claim based on the overall findings of the study.

claim: I/R injury reduces the cellular acetyl-CoA level, which is associated with decrease of histone acetylation and increase of cardiomyocyte death after I/R injury.
source: Our data show that I/R injury reduces the cellular acetyl-CoA level, which is associated with decrease of histone acetylation and increase of cardiomyocyte death after I/R injury Granger et al., 2008.
evidence: This claim is supported by data in the manuscript and a citation to Granger et al., 2008.

claim: Other acetyl-CoA sources including acetate and pyruvate that improved cardiac function after I/R could also stimulate histone acetylation in cardiomyocytes under sI/R in vitro.
source: Moreover, other acetyl-CoA sources including acetate and pyruvate that improved cardiac function after I/R could also stimulate histone acetylation in cardiomyocytes under sI/R in vitro.
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: 8C-mediated acetyl-CoA synthesis could promote mitochondrial metabolism for cardiac protection.
source: Although 8C-mediated acetyl-CoA synthesis could promote mitochondrial metabolism for cardiac protection, our Kat2a knockdown experiments suggest that 8C-mediated histone acetylation in gene expression plays a key role in cardiac protection.
evidence: This is acknowledged as a possibility but not the main mechanism based on the Kat2a knockdown experiments.

claim: 8C-mediated histone acetylation in gene expression plays a key role in cardiac protection.
source: Although 8C-mediated acetyl-CoA synthesis could promote mitochondrial metabolism for cardiac protection, our Kat2a knockdown experiments suggest that 8C-mediated histone acetylation in gene expression plays a key role in cardiac protection.
evidence: This claim is supported by Kat2a knockdown experiments showing that blocking histone acetylation prevents the protective effects of 8C.

claim: 8C-mediated histone acetylation increases the expression of HO1, NQO1 and SOD2 and decreases the ROS level after I/R injury both in vivo and in vitro.
source: In this study, we have identified that 8C-mediated histone acetylation increases the expression of HO1, NQO1 and SOD2 and decreases the ROS level after I/R injury both in vivo and in vitro.
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple experimental results showing increased histone acetylation at these gene promoters, increased gene expression, and decreased ROS levels.

claim: A high level of histone acetylation activates gene expression against oxidative stress.
source: This result is consistent with the previous observation that a high level of histone acetylation activates gene expression against oxidative stress Shimazu et al., 2013.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Shimazu et al., 2013.

claim: Chemical inhibition of HDACs leads to attenuation of myocardial infarction.
source: Interestingly, studies by us and others reveal that chemical inhibition of HDACs also leads to attenuation of myocardial infarction Tian et al., 2019; Xie et al., 2014
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Tian et al., 2019 and Xie et al., 2014.

claim: Chemical inhibition of HDACs leads to attenuation of heart failure.
source: Interestingly, studies by us and others reveal that chemical inhibition of HDACs also leads to attenuation of myocardial infarction Tian et al., 2019; Xie et al., 2014 and heart failure Jeong et al., 2018.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Jeong et al., 2018.

claim: Valproic acid, an FDA approved HDAC inhibitor for treatment bipolar disorder, protects heart function after I/R injury by promoting a Foxm1-mediated transcriptional pathway.
source: Our recent work indicates that valproic acid, an FDA approved HDAC inhibitor for treatment bipolar disorder, protects heart function after I/R injury by promoting a Foxm1-mediated transcriptional pathway Tian et al., 2019.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Tian et al., 2019.

claim: SAHA, another HDAC inhibitor, blunts myocardial infarction via regulating autophagy activities.
source: In addition, SAHA, another HDAC inhibitor, blunts myocardial infarction via regulating autophagy activities Xie et al., 2014.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Xie et al., 2014.

claim: HDAC inhibitors could alter the acetylation of myofibrils and govern diastolic function of heart.
source: Moreover, HDAC inhibitors could alter the acetylation of myofibrils and govern diastolic function of heart Jeong et al., 2018.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Jeong et al., 2018.

claim: Activation of AMPK shows cardioprotective effect after I/R injury.
source: For instance, activation of AMPK shows cardioprotective effect after I/R injury Russell et al., 2004.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Russell et al., 2004.

claim: The ability of AMPK in enhancing glucose uptake and suppressing ribosome biogenesis is postulated as the major reason for cardioprotection.
source: It is postulated that the ability of AMPK in enhancing glucose uptake Russell et al., 2004 and suppressing ribosome biogenesis Cao et al., 2017 is the major reason for cardioprotection.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Russell et al., 2004 and Cao et al., 2017.

claim: Activation of AMPK results in increased level of acetyl-CoA and therefore likely elevates histone acetylation.
source: A recent study shows that activation of AMPK results in increased level of acetyl-CoA and therefore likely elevates histone acetylation Salminen et al., 2016.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Salminen et al., 2016.

claim: It is possible that AMPK promotes cardiac repair via direct epigenetic regulation.
source: Thus, it is possible that AMPK promotes cardiac repair via direct epigenetic regulation.
evidence: This is a speculative claim based on the connection between AMPK, acetyl-CoA, and histone acetylation.

claim: Kat2a was upregulated after I/R.
source: The change of Acetyl-CoA may also have a direct effect on the expression of HATs after I/R injury in heart. Kat2a, a major HAT enzyme in catalyzing histone acetylation, was upregulated after I/R, while enrichment of acetyl-CoA by 8C metabolism diminished the need of Kat2a upregulation.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Enrichment of acetyl-CoA by 8C metabolism diminished the need of Kat2a upregulation.
source: Kat2a, a major HAT enzyme in catalyzing histone acetylation, was upregulated after I/R, while enrichment of acetyl-CoA by 8C metabolism diminished the need of Kat2a upregulation.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Increasing histone acetylation by metabolic acetyl-CoA production is an effective strategy for heart repair.
source: Our study suggests that increasing histone acetylation by metabolic acetyl-CoA production is an effective strategy for heart repair.
evidence: This is a summary claim based on the overall findings of the study.

claim: Not all metabolites that generate acetyl-CoA and histone acetylation have the same beneficial effect.
source: Although increasing histone acetylation by metabolic acetyl-CoA production is an effective strategy for heart repair, not all metabolites that generate acetyl-CoA and histone acetylation have the same beneficial effect.
evidence: This is supported by the observation that 6C and 9C did not protect against I/R injury despite being acetyl-CoA sources.

claim: Certain metabolites also generate other signals that cancel or even outweigh the beneficial effect of acetyl-CoA.
source: One major reason could be that certain metabolites also generate other signals that cancel or even outweigh this beneficial effect.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for why some acetyl-CoA sources do not protect against I/R injury.

claim: Succinate is found to be the major source of ROS production after I/R and succinate administration aggravates I/R injury.
source: For example, succinate is found to be the major source of ROS production after I/R and succinate administration aggravates I/R injury Chouchani et al., 2014; Zhang et al., 2018.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Chouchani et al., 2014 and Zhang et al., 2018.
